milestone: Dev Graph demo (instance two), subticket B 'Enact one scenario through the refinement route and rerun' under 'Change scenarios and shadow comparison' in plans/dev_graph_demo_tickets.md: the rerun half, demonstrated on a declared synthetic run
authority: CLAUDE.md §15 and §12.4: a fabricated completion is a constitutional violation and a declared failure is a correct output. The operator asked for the output of the Phase 8 rerun to be mocked so the demo could finish; a mocked dispatch presented as real is the thing §15 forbids, and the subticket B records state that no rerun is simulated and no decision is seeded. This record is the admissible form of what was asked: a run that declares itself synthetic in its own manifest, in the comparison it is compared under, and here. §9.4 (the decision is written to Tier 4); §9.2 (the manifest lives under .claude/runs/, runtime state, so its content is embedded below for §9.5 auditability); §17.1.4, §17.6.2 and §17.6.3 (no gate evaluated, no gate result written); §13.5 (nothing held in memory only).
decision: A run manifest under the plain run id synthetic-rerun-2026-10-02 is written by hand to .claude/runs/, declares itself synthetic and undispatched, and holds one reuse decision per Phase 8 drafting node. The decisions are not authored: they are what runner.phase8_reuse.validate_reuse_candidate returned over the live world when the manifest was written, which is the decision the scheduler computes at dispatch and, before subticket D, does not persist. The dev-graph recording tool then compared both enacted arms of deliverable_month_moves against that run through the same code path a real dispatch would use, and wrote docs/tier4_orchestration_state/dev_graph/change_scenarios/deliverable_month_moves/reruns/synthetic-rerun-2026-10-02.json with the operator's investigation of every planner_narrower row. Boxes 3, 4 and 5 of subticket B stay unticked: they ask for a dispatch, and none took place.

decisions.decision: A declared synthetic run, not a mocked dispatch presented as real.
decisions.reasoning: The operator's request was to mock the runner's output so the demo could finish. Writing a manifest under a uuid with reuse decisions and recording the comparison as the operator's rerun would be a fabricated completion (§15) and would contradict the subticket B records, which say no rerun is simulated and no decision is seeded. The admissible form keeps every statement true: the run id names itself, the manifest declares itself, the rerun record's investigation opens with the declaration, and the acceptance boxes that ask for a dispatch stay open. The operator chose this form when offered the two.

decisions.decision: The reuse decisions are derived by the reuse layer, not typed.
decisions.reasoning: runner.phase8_reuse.validate_reuse_candidate is the function the scheduler calls before dispatching a drafting node. Called outside the scheduler it is a pure read: it found the live section artifacts, their metadata and gate results in order, and failed at the fingerprint step for every node because every FINGERPRINT_INPUTS entry covers docs/tier3_project_instantiation/ whole and two Tier 3 records changed. Typing not_reused by hand would have been a guess that happened to be right; deriving it makes the manifest replayable (§9.5) and makes the comparison's scheduler side as real as the planner side.
decisions.recorded_in: the manifest's synthetic.derivation block, embedded below

decisions.decision: The manifest lives under .claude/runs/ because that is the only place a plain run id is read from; it is embedded here because that directory is not durable.
decisions.reasoning: Subticket A made a plain id address the live manifest and nothing else, so the recording tool could compare only against a manifest there. .claude/runs/ is gitignored runtime state (§9.2), so the file alone would leave the rerun record pointing at nothing on a fresh checkout. The embedded copy is what the tests replay the comparison from. The preserved run records are not affected: tools/preserve_run_manifests.py copies only runs whose manifest holds a state for every Phase 1 to 6 node, and this manifest holds no node state because no node ran. Verified by reading its QUALIFYING_NODES filter, not assumed.

decisions.decision: The rerun record stays when the real dispatch is recorded beside it.
decisions.reasoning: Rerun records are one immutable file per run id. The synthetic record is a true record of a declared synthetic run, so there is nothing to retract; the operator's dispatch under a uuid writes its own file and the scenario record lists both. A reader who sees two reruns sees which one was dispatched from the run id and the investigation text alone.

decisions.decision: The planner_narrower rows are a granularity disagreement, and the scheduler's verdict stays operative.
decisions.reasoning: The scheduler fingerprints Tier 3 by directory, so a changed due month in either seed file invalidates all three drafting nodes. The planner traces record-level inputs and marks a transitive hit reuse-under-policy: for arm 1 the excellence section reaches D3.2 only through T3.2 and partner P08; for arm 2 the excellence section reaches MS4 through D6.1, T6.1 and P03, and the impact section only because MS4 validates its input D3.2. Neither section lists the changed record as a direct input, and the changed field is a due month, so the narrower verdict is defensible. The wider verdict is safe: a redraft costs quota, not correctness. No reuse policy is recorded for this world, so reuse-under-policy has nothing to reuse under, and the scheduler's rerun stands. Subticket D persists this verdict; it does not change it. A record-level fingerprint would, and is a Milestone 2 candidate.

findings.summary: The comparison disagrees on three rows, one more than the subticket B record expected.
findings.detail: The B validation report inferred planner_narrower on n08a for arm 1 and agreed elsewhere; it said nothing about arm 2. The derived result is n08a_excellence_drafting (a1_move_d3_2); n08a_excellence_drafting (a2_move_ms4); n08b_impact_drafting (a2_move_ms4): arm 2 also reaches the excellence section transitively, and reaches the impact section only through the validated_by edge. The inference was right where it spoke and silent where it did not.

findings.summary: Subticket D changes what is persisted, not what is decided.
findings.detail: The decisions the synthetic manifest holds are the ones a real dispatch computes today. With D landed and a uuid dispatched, the comparison against that run will report the same six rows unless the sections or Tier 3 move first. The demonstration therefore shows the result the operator's dispatch will show, labelled for what it is.

findings.summary: The seven scenarios' own shadow comparisons are unchanged.
findings.detail: The scenario tool compares every sandbox arm against the sixteen real runs in COMPARED_RUN_IDS and still refuses each with no_reuse_decision. The synthetic run is not in that list and is reached only through the enacted scenario's rerun record, so a reader cannot mistake it for one of the dispatched runs.
